gaps.sentence: We stopped at a cafe to ___ a chat.
gaps.explanation: have a chat is the fixed collocation for a friendly, informal conversation.

gaps.sentence: I ___ a strange dream last night.
gaps.explanation: have a dream is the English collocation; 'see a dream' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: The wedding will ___ place in the village church.
gaps.explanation: take place means to happen; it is the fixed phrase for events.

gaps.sentence: My brother and I ___ turns washing up after dinner.
gaps.explanation: take turns means to do something one after another, alternating.

gaps.sentence: Try to ___ quiet — the exam is in progress.
gaps.explanation: keep quiet means to stay silent; 'make quiet' is not used.

gaps.sentence: We were asked to ___ an experiment in the laboratory.
gaps.explanation: do an experiment is the standard collocation in scientific contexts.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: We ___ breakfast on the terrace every morning in summer.
gaps.explanation: have breakfast/lunch/dinner is the standard collocation for eating meals.
